inputTooltips.measure: The numeric metric this strategy should analyze, such as revenue, cost, or a count.
inputTooltips.timeDimension: The date or time field used to order results, such as order date or meeting date.
inputTooltips.dimensions: The categories to break the result down by, such as region, product, or customer.
inputTooltips.filters: Fields that limit which records are included, such as status or a date range.
inputTooltips.interval: Choose how time is grouped, such as day, week, month, or quarter.
inputTooltips.baseline: The reference value or period the result is compared against.
inputTooltips.currentPeriod: The period to look at now, such as this month or this quarter.
inputTooltips.comparisonPeriod: The earlier period to compare against, such as last month or the same month last year.
inputTooltips.timeRange: The start and end of the time window this analysis should cover.
inputTooltips.comparisonPeriods: The pair of periods used to measure change, such as this quarter and last quarter.
inputTooltips.topN: Set how many of the highest or lowest results to keep, such as the top 10.
inputTooltips.binDefinition: Describe how numeric values are grouped into ranges, such as 0–100, 100–500, and 500+.
inputTooltips.percentiles: Choose which percentile cutoffs to calculate, such as the 25th, 50th, and 90th.
inputTooltips.outcomeMeasure: The result you want to explain, such as cancellations, failures, or wins.
inputTooltips.reasonDimension: The field that records why something happened, such as a reason code or cancellation cause.
inputTooltips.baselineDefinition: Describe how the normal or expected value is calculated before looking for unusual results.
inputTooltips.method: Choose the calculation or statistical method, such as a correlation type or an outlier rule.
inputTooltips.threshold: Set the cutoff that decides when a value counts as unusual or out of range.
inputTooltips.minimumSampleSize: Set the smallest number of records required before a result is trusted.
inputTooltips.targetContributionPercentage: Set the share of the total you want the top groups to explain, such as 80%.
inputTooltips.concentrationThreshold: Set the share held by a few entities that should be flagged as concentrated risk.
inputTooltips.benchmark: The target, budget, SLA, or peer value the actual result is compared with.
inputTooltips.tolerance: Set how far from the target a result can be and still count as acceptable.
inputTooltips.startingValue: The beginning amount in a waterfall, before any changes are applied.
inputTooltips.endingValue: The final amount the waterfall should reach after all changes.
inputTooltips.changeComponents: The individual increases and decreases that bridge the start value to the end value.
inputTooltips.actualMeasure: The measure of what actually happened, such as actual sales or actual hours.
inputTooltips.targetMeasure: The measure of the goal or expected result, such as a target, budget, or quota.
inputTooltips.accumulationWindow: Choose the period a running total resets over, such as year to date or month to date.
inputTooltips.entityIdentifier: The field that identifies each person, account, or item, such as customer id.
inputTooltips.cohortDefinition: Describe the shared starting event that groups entities together, such as signup month.
inputTooltips.followUpPeriod: Set how long after the starting event each group is observed, such as 30, 60, or 90 days.
inputTooltips.processModel: The workflow whose stages should be analyzed, such as an order or hiring process.
inputTooltips.orderedStages: List the stages in the order they happen, such as lead, qualified, proposal, and closed.
inputTooltips.activityDefinition: Describe what counts as activity, such as a login, purchase, or meeting.
inputTooltips.retentionWindow: Set the time span used to decide whether an entity stayed active, such as 30 days.
inputTooltips.numericMeasures: At least two numeric measures whose relationship you want to test.
inputTooltips.inputMeasure: The driver whose change you want to test, such as price or discount.
inputTooltips.model: Describe the formula or model that relates the input to the outcome.
inputTooltips.scenarioRange: Set the range of input changes to try, such as price from -10% to +10%.
inputTooltips.numeratorMeasure: The top of a ratio, such as profit in a margin or completions in a rate.
inputTooltips.denominatorMeasure: The bottom of a ratio, such as revenue in a margin or attempts in a rate.
inputTooltips.capacityMeasure: The maximum the process can handle, such as available seats or staff hours.
inputTooltips.dimensionA: The first category in a cross-tab, shown as rows, such as region.
inputTooltips.dimensionB: The second category in a cross-tab, shown as columns, such as product.
inputTooltips.cycleType: Choose the repeating calendar cycle to look for, such as day of week, month, or quarter.
inputTooltips.smoothingMethod: Choose how noisy values are smoothed before measuring change, such as a moving average.
inputTooltips.activityDate: The date of each activity used to measure how recent and how frequent it is.
inputTooltips.asOfDate: The reference date age or recency is measured from.
inputTooltips.frequencyWindow: Set the time span used to count how often an activity happened.
inputTooltips.numberOfTiers: Set how many groups to split entities into, such as 4 quartiles or 10 deciles.
inputTooltips.tierBoundaries: Set the cutoff values that separate tiers when the groups should not be equal sized.
inputTooltips.thresholdRule: Describe the rule that decides a breach, such as a value above 100 or below an SLA.
inputTooltips.severityRules: Describe how breaches are ranked, such as warning versus critical.
inputTooltips.baselineModel: Describe the expected pattern used to spot anomalies, such as a trailing average or a seasonal baseline.
inputTooltips.sensitivity: Set how readily a small deviation is flagged. Higher sensitivity raises more alerts.
inputTooltips.seasonality: Say whether repeating calendar patterns, such as weekends or holidays, should be accounted for.
inputTooltips.dimensionHierarchy: The levels to drill through, from broad to detailed, such as region, then city, then store.
inputTooltips.targetCondition: Describe the situation to investigate, such as a decrease in revenue or a metric below target.
inputTooltips.maximumDepth: Set how many hierarchy levels the drill-down may go through before it stops.
inputTooltips.observationIdentifier: The unit that groups items occurring together, such as an order id or a basket.
inputTooltips.itemOrEvent: The thing that can appear together inside that unit, such as a product or an event type.
inputTooltips.minimumSupport: Set how often an item set must appear before it is kept. Rare combinations are excluded.
inputTooltips.minimumConfidence: Set how often the second item must follow the first before the pair is kept.
inputTooltips.minimumLift: Set how much more often the pair must occur than chance. Values near 1 are weak associations.
inputTooltips.startDate: The date an item was created or entered the state being aged.
inputTooltips.currentStatus: The status that marks an item as still open, such as pending or in progress.
inputTooltips.agingBuckets: Set the age ranges to group open items into, such as 0–30, 31–60, and 60+ days.
inputTooltips.forecastHorizon: Set how far ahead to project, such as the rest of the month or the next quarter.
inputTooltips.currentPeriodProgress: Set how much of the current period has already elapsed, used to judge the current pace.
inputTooltips.historicalPeriods: Set how many past periods to use when estimating the future, such as the last 12 months.
inputTooltips.scenarioParameters: The inputs you want to change in a what-if, such as price, volume, or headcount.
inputTooltips.calculationModel: Describe the formula that turns those inputs into the target metric.
inputTooltips.baselineScenario: Describe the starting case other scenarios are compared with, usually the current plan.
inputTooltips.constraints: Describe limits the scenario must respect, such as a budget cap or a capacity limit.
inputTooltips.parameterRanges: Set the allowed values for each scenario input, such as a minimum and maximum price.
